verdict.summary: Accessing remains technically close to RC quality, with strong authentication-focused product definition, Symfony-oriented architecture, modern runtime dependencies, and substantial QA tooling, but the assessed state is still an untagged refactor branch with a dirty working tree and a transitional gating migration.
strengths: Authentication and identity responsibilities are explicitly documented through product, architecture, bounding, audit, and full manifests.
The implementation targets PHP 8.4 and Symfony 8.1 with dedicated security, WebAuthn, OTP, rate-limiting, validation, serialization, mailer, and notifier capabilities.
QA infrastructure includes PHPUnit 12, PHPStan 2.1, PHP CS Fixer, coverage tooling, Panther, and Playwright.
Recent commits show active canonicalization and RC-oriented test coverage work.
risks: The assessed HEAD is on refactor/accessing-canonical-structure and has no exact release tag.
The working tree contains modified and untracked authentication tests, so the QA baseline is not reproducible from HEAD alone.
The .gating area contains deleted tracked configuration alongside extensive untracked replacement content.
RC confidence remains dependent on reconciliation and verification of the final committed state.
next_actions: Reconcile and commit the intended gating migration.
Reconcile the pending authentication test changes and additions.
Run the repository's full lint, coding-standard, PHPStan, PHPUnit, coverage, Panther, and applicable Playwright gates on the resulting clean tree.
Merge the canonical refactor into the intended release branch and create an immutable verified RC tag.
Refresh the Quality Atlas snapshot from that clean tagged commit.
notes: The repository facts support preserving the existing scores because the principal RC blockers identified by the current snapshot remain present.
No score increase is justified until the dirty working tree, transitional gating state, and lack of an exact tag are resolved.
